Description: "The axTLS embedded SSL project is a highly configurable client/server TLSv1.2 library designed for platforms with small memory requirements. It comes with a small HTTP/HTTPS server and additional test tools." ([source](https://axtls.sourceforge.net/))
System Software: intended to be built for platforms with limited resources ([source](https://axtls.sourceforge.net/))
Notes: "The build mechanism uses mconf which is tool similar to that used with BusyBox and the Linux kernel' ([source](https://axtls.sourceforge.net/faq.htm))

Description: "A bootloader that follows the tradition of Das U-Boot, while adopting modern design ideas from the Linux kernel." ([source](https://github.com/barebox/barebox/blob/master/README.rst))
System Software: "barebox aims to be a versatile and flexible bootloader, not only for booting embedded Linux systems, but also for initial hardware bringup and development. barebox is highly configurable to be suitable as a full-featured development binary as well as for lean production systems. Just like busybox is the Swiss Army Knife for embedded Linux, barebox is the Swiss Army Knife for bare metal, hence the name." ([source](https://barebox.org/))
Notes: occasionally re-synced to the Linux implementation (currently [6.18](https://github.com/barebox/barebox/commit/243abef11b8f69e2595ce55e64786c99c5d8e8fe))

Description: "Buildroot is a simple, efficient and easy-to-use tool to generate embedded Linux systems through cross-compilation." ([source](https://buildroot.org/))\n "Buildroot is a set of Makefiles and patches that makes it easy generate a cross-compilation toolchain and root filesystem for your target Linux system using the uClibc C library." ([source](https://buildroot.org/news.html))
System Software: "Buildroot is useful mainly for people working with small or embedded systems." ([source](https://buildroot.org/news.html)) "making it a first class citizen of uclibc.org and busybox.net" it is a consumer of these projects: BusyBox, uClibc, Linux kernel, Barebox, U-Boot (and therefore may be considered a multi product line)
Notes: "This is a copy of the kconfig code in the kernel (.currently 4.17-rc2) tweaked to suit Buildroot." ([source](https://github.com/buildroot/buildroot/tree/master/support/kconfig)) "Buildroot has a nice configuration tool similar to the one you can find in the Linux kernel or in BusyBox." ([source](https://buildroot.org/downloads/manual/manual.html)) "Very easy to set up, thanks to its menuconfig, gconfig, and xconfig configuration interfaces, familiar to all embedded Linux developers" ([source](https://linuxgizmos.com/buildroot-project-reports-progress-releases-update/)) build route includes a set of patches to apply to LKC ([source](https://github.com/buildroot/buildroot/tree/master/support/kconfig/patches)) ([source](https://youtu.be/0G_yJ50RA3I?t=287))

Description: "BusyBox combines tiny versions of many common UNIX utilities into a single small executable. It provides replacements for most of the utilities you usually find in GNU fileutils, shellutils, etc." ([source](https://busybox.net/about.html))\n "BusyBox is a set of command-line utilities developed with the goal of keeping its size as small as possible. To that end, all unnecessary options and code are ruthlessly cut out, and the entire command set is implemented by a single, multipurpose executable. BusyBox is found in a number of embedded environments; chances are it is running on your wireless router, for example." ([source](https://lwn.net/Articles/202106/))
System Software: "BusyBox provides a fairly complete environment for any small or embedded system." "BusyBox has been written with size-optimization and limited resources in mind." ([source](https://busybox.net/about.html)) it is intended to be cross compiled ([source](https://busybox.net/FAQ.html)), "minimize run-time memory usage (heap and stack), run fast"
Notes: "Busybox uses the same "menuconfig" infrastructure as the Linux kernel" ([source](https://busybox.net/FAQ.html))

Description: "coreboot is a Free Software project aimed at replacing the proprietary firmware (BIOS/UEFI) found in most computers. coreboot performs the required hardware initialization to configure the system, then passes control to a different executable, referred to in coreboot as the payload. Most often, the primary function of the payload is to boot the operating system (OS). ([source](https://github.com/coreboot/coreboot/blob/master/README.md))"
System Software: "coreboot is perfect for a wide variety of situations. It can be used for specialized applications that run directly in the firmware, running operating systems from flash, loading custom bootloaders, or implementing firmware standards, like PC BIOS services or UEFI." ([source](https://github.com/coreboot/coreboot/blob/master/README.md)) "coreboot is an alternative to BIOS and deals mainly with motherboards" ([source](https://dl.acm.org/doi/pdf/10.1145/3551349.3556899)) "Tesla Is Making Use Of The Open-Source Coreboot Within Their Electric Vehicles" ([source](https://www.phoronix.com/news/Tesla-Uses-Coreboot))
Notes: "This is coreboot's copy of kconfig which tracks Linux as upstream but comes with a few patches for portability but also a few semantic changes." ([source](https://github.com/coreboot/coreboot/tree/master/util/kconfig)) applies [patches](https://github.com/coreboot/coreboot/tree/master/util/kconfig/patches) to LKC

Description: "Crosstool-NG is a versatile (cross) toolchain generator. It supports many architectures and components and has a simple yet powerful menuconfig-style interface." ([source](https://crosstool-ng.github.io/))
System Software: "Toolchains are an essential component in a software development project. It will compile, assemble and link the code that is being developed." ([source](https://crosstool-ng.github.io/docs/introduction/))
Notes: occasionally re-synced to the Linux implementation (currently [5.9](https://github.com/crosstool-ng/crosstool-ng/commit/d0e328c8ad357a705b6218e20f74ec1ec1869e8d))

Description: "EmbToolkit eases setup of necessary tools for embedded linux system development, including the root filesystem generation. It generates toolchain/SDK based on traditional GNU tools (GCC, Binutils, etc.) and/or the newer clang/llvm compiler infrastructure." ([source](https://embtoolkit.org/))
System Software: not run itself on an embedded system, but assists embedded development "EmbToolkit will be handy if you want to develop applications and generate firmware for a highly customized/specialized embedded linux product." ([source](https://embtoolkit.org/))
Notes: "Easy configuration interface through menuconfig or xconfig, like the linux kernel." ([source](https://embtoolkit.org/)) "foo.kconfig: a configuration file which uses the simple linux kernel kconfig language" "This file syntax is the same as linux kconfig" ([source](https://embtoolkit.org/userguide.html))

Description: Entware is a software repository for embedded devices which use the Linux kernel, such as routers and network-attached storage (NAS) devices." ([source](https://github.com/Entware/Entware/wiki))
System Software: "Currently different Entware versions are widely used in routers, NASes, Android devices and other hardware that uses Linux kernel." ([source](https://bin.entware.net/Readme.txt)) "Ultimate repo for embedded devices" ([source](https://github.com/Entware/entware/))
Notes: occasionally re-synced to OpenWrt's implementation (currently [6.6.16](https://github.com/Entware/Entware/blob/969c703e6fd8b2ad84d82affaeb14b48d1fcb105/scripts/config/README))

Description: Freetz-NG (a fork of Freetz) is a firmware-extension (modification) for the AVM Fritz!Box and devices with identical hardware. The original firmware from the manufacturer is extended with new functions and programs which may be selected by the user. Freetz-NG uses trunk-based development - there are some tags and inconsistent old releases, but they do not cover the entire history. ([source](https://freetz-ng.github.io/freetz-ng/NEWS/))
System Software: Firmware: "Freetz is a toolbox for developers and experienced users to build a modified firmware based on the original firmware for the DSL/LAN/WLAN/VoIP-Routers ​AVM Fritz!Box and ​T-Com Speedport (identical hardware) and to transfer this firmware to the device." ([source](https://freetz.github.io/wiki/FAQ.en.html)); includes a copy of the feature model of BusyBox and other systems, as well as many own features (and thus may be considered a multi product line)
Notes: "The description comes from the documentation of the Linux kernel, from which we (and other open-source projects) have borrowed this type of MK and the necessary tools." ([source](https://freetz.github.io/wiki/help/howtos/development/menuconfig.html)); "To configure Freetz it makes use of conf/mconf, which some or other already knows from the linux kernel configuration" ([source](https://freetz.github.io/wiki/FAQ.en.html))

Description: "L4Re is an operating system framework that allows you to build custom operating system and hypervisor solutions." ([source](https://l4re.org/overview/))\n "Architecturally, L4Re is a microkernel-based operating system." ([source](https://l4re.org/overview/architecture.html))
System Software: "The L4Re Microkernel is both suitable for big and complex systems as well as small, embedded applications." ([source](https://os.inf.tu-dresden.de/fiasco/)) multi-architecture support like Linux ([source](https://os.inf.tu-dresden.de/fiasco/features.html)) intended for safety and security critical systems ([source](https://l4re.org/overview/usecases.html)) "L4 is widely deployed. One variant, OKL4 from Open Kernel Labs, shipped in billions of mobile devices" ([source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L4_microkernel_family))
Notes: "kconfig taken from vanilla Linux 6.17, and slightly patched." ([source](https://github.com/kernkonzept/fiasco/tree/master/tool/kconfig))

Description: "Linux is a clone of the operating system Unix, written from scratch by Linus Torvalds with assistance from a loosely-knit team of hackers across the Net. It aims towards POSIX and Single UNIX Specification compliance. It has all the features you would expect in a modern fully-fledged Unix, including true multitasking, virtual memory, shared libraries, demand loading, shared copy-on-write executables, proper memory management, and multistack networking including IPv4 and IPv6." ([source](https://www.kernel.org/doc/Documentation/admin-guide/README.rst))
System Software: "Linux is easily portable to most general-purpose 32- or 64-bit architectures as long as they have a paged memory management unit (PMMU) and a port of the GNU C compiler (gcc) (part of The GNU Compiler Collection, GCC)." ([source](https://www.kernel.org/doc/Documentation/admin-guide/README.rst))
Notes: original Kconfig implementation, which incepted this configuration language

Description: OpenADK is a "menu based buildsystem for your embedded Linux system" ([source](https://github.com/wbx-github/openadk/blob/master/README/)) and a "free construction kit for Embedded Devices. The resulting firmware boots up very fast, is updateable without losing local configuration changes and the root filesystem is mounted read-only. The default configuration creates a very small linux system." ([source](https://openadk.org/))
System Software: "A free construction kit for Embedded Devices. The resulting firmware boots up very fast, is updateable without losing local configuration changes and the root filesystem is mounted read-only. The default configuration creates a very small linux system." ([source](https://openadk.org/))
Notes: uses a 2014 version of the Linux implementation ([source](https://github.com/wbx-github/openadk/commit/949d8663f2f12c986ef2983b7b307f5ecddf060e))

Description: "The OpenWrt Project is a Linux operating system targeting embedded devices." ([source](https://github.com/openwrt/openwrt/blob/main/README.md))
System Software: "OpenWrt is a highly extensible GNU/Linux distribution for embedded devices (typically wireless routers). Unlike many other distributions for routers, OpenWrt is built from the ground up to be a full-featured, easily modifiable operating system for embedded devices. In practice, this means that you can have all the features you need with none of the bloat, powered by a modern Linux kernel." ([source](https://openwrt.org/docs/start))
Notes: occasionally re-synced to the Linux implementation (currently [6.6.16](https://github.com/openwrt/openwrt/blob/main/scripts/config/README)) applies [patches](https://github.com/cotequeiroz/linux/commits/openwrt-v6.6.16/scripts/kconfig) to LKC

Description: "PTXdist is a build system for firmware images. It is developed by an Open Source Community including Pengutronix since 2001." ([source](https://www.ptxdist.org/))
System Software: "PTXdist is a build system which can be used to generate a root tree and disk images for all kinds of Linux systems. It was written with embedded systems in mind, but there is no reason why you can't use it to configure your firewall, router or whatever dedicated device" comes to your mind."" ([source](https://git.pengutronix.de/cgit/ptxdist/tree/README))"
Notes: "The configuration system Kconfig, known from the Linux kernel, is used to select and configure each package." ([source](https://www.ptxdist.org/)) "This is a copy of the linux-2.6.28 scripts/kconfig directory." ([source](https://git.pengutronix.de/cgit/ptxdist/tree/scripts/kconfig/README.PTX)) applies [patches](https://git.pengutronix.de/cgit/ptxdist/tree/scripts/ptx-modifications) to LKC

Description: "QEMU is a generic and open source machine & userspace emulator and virtualizer." ([source](https://gitlab.com/qemu-project/qemu/-/blob/master/README.rst))
System Software: "QEMU is capable of emulating a complete machine in software without any need for hardware virtualization support. By using dynamic translation, it achieves very good performance. [...] When QEMU emulates CPUs directly it is capable of running operating systems made for one machine (e.g. an ARMv7 board) on a different machine (e.g. an x86_64 PC board)." ([source](https://gitlab.com/qemu-project/qemu/-/blob/master/README.rst)) "QEMU is a very versatile emulator; it can be built for a variety of targets, where each target can emulate various boards and at the same time different targets can share large amounts of code" ([source](https://www.qemu.org/docs/master/devel/kconfig.html))
Notes: "QEMU uses a simple domain-specific language to describe the dependencies between components. [...] This domain-specific language is based on the Kconfig language that originated in the Linux kernel, though it was heavily simplified and the handling of dependencies is stricter in QEMU." ([source](https://www.qemu.org/docs/master/devel/kconfig.html))

Description: "Soletta Project is a framework for making IoT devices. With Soletta Project's libraries developers can easily write software for devices that control actuators/sensors and communicate using standard technologies." ([source](https://github.com/solettaproject/soletta/blob/master/README.md))
System Software: "Soletta works on top of many different operating systems and features supported on each of these systems may differ. Aside from Linux, they are focused on Embedded Systems and IoT." ([source](https://github.com/solettaproject/soletta/blob/master/README.md))
Notes: "The build system is based on linux kernel's kconfig." ([source](https://github.com/solettaproject/soletta/blob/master/README.kconfig)) uses the Linux 4.0 implementation ([source](https://github.com/solettaproject/soletta/commit/48831700d0f480dde4a55d2998b1d7c91964f1cb))

Description: "Toybox combines many common Linux command line utilities together into a single BSD-licensed executable. Toybox's main goal is to make Android self-hosting by improving Android's command line utilities so it can build an installable Android Open Source Project image entirely from source under a stock Android system." It is similar to BusyBox and was created by BusyBox's maintainer due to a licensing argument. (Source [1](https://landley.net/toybox/), [2](https://landley.net/talks/elc-2019.txt), [3](https://landley.net/toybox/faq.html#why_toybox), [4](https://lwn.net/Articles/202106/))
System Software: Intended to make android (an operating system) self-hosting, intended to be cross-compiled, intended for constrained environments (like embedded systems) where fork() is unavailable, only depends on libc ([source](https://landley.net/toybox/faq.html))
Notes: "copied from the Linux kernel" ([source](https://landley.net/toybox/faq.html#code)) "This is a snapshot of linux 2.6.12 kconfig as washed through busybox and further modified by Rob Landley." He had a hard time getting changes upstream: ([source](https://github.com/landley/toybox/tree/master/kconfig)) Due to this and licensing issues (LKC is GPL) he is rewriting a Kconfig implementation from scratch for version 1.0: "This development cycle finally started replacing the old kconfig/*.c plumbing (dating back to the 2.6 kernel) with a new scripts/kconfig.c" ([source](https://landley.net/toybox/news.html))

Description: U-Boot is "a boot loader for Embedded boards based on PowerPC, ARM, MIPS and several other processors." ([source](https://github.com/u-boot/u-boot/blob/master/README))
System Software: "can be installed in a boot ROM and used to initialize and test the hardware or to download and run application code" ([source](https://github.com/u-boot/u-boot/blob/master/README)) used in Raspberry Pi 4 ([source](https://docs.u-boot.org/en/stable/board/broadcom/raspberrypi.html))
Notes: "The conventional configuration was replaced by Kconfig at v2014.10-rc1 release." ([source](https://github.com/u-boot/u-boot/blob/master/doc/develop/kconfig.rst)) occasionally re-synced to the Linux implementation (currently [4.20](https://github.com/u-boot/u-boot/commit/473fc279c898d113cc5eff656efbbf08e1bea1d3)) Masahiro Yamada, a core developer of U-Boot, was also maintainer of KConfig in the Linux kernel from 2018-2025

Description: "uClibc (aka µClibc/pronounced yew-see-lib-see) is a C library for developing embedded Linux systems. It is much smaller than the GNU C Library, but nearly all applications supported by glibc also work perfectly with uClibc." ([source](https://web.archive.org/web/20250501014431/https://www.uclibc.org/about.html))
System Software: "Initially, the project began since the GNU C library lacked support for MMU-less systems, and because glibc is very large." "intended primarily for embedded use" also has cross compilation support ([source](https://web.archive.org/web/20250613192936/https://uclibc.org/FAQ.html))
Notes: "This is a copy of the kconfig code in the kernel tweaked to suit uClibc" ([source](https://github.com/kraj/uClibc/tree/master/extra/config))

Description: uClibc++ is a C++ standard library targeted towards the embedded systems/software market." ([source](https://cxx.uclibc.org/about.html))
System Software: uClibc++ "may purposefully lack features which you might normally expect to find in a full fledged C++ standard library. The library will focus on space savings as opposed to performance."" ([source](https://cxx.uclibc.org/about.html))"
Notes: presumably uses a 2008 version of the Linux implementation

Description: "uClibc-ng is a small C library for developing embedded Linux systems. It is much smaller than the GNU C Library, but nearly all applications supported by glibc also work perfectly with uClibc-ng." This is a fork of uclibc and was started after its last release. We include it here separately because its repository does not include the history of uClibc. ([source](https://github.com/brgl/uclibc-ng/blob/master/README))
System Software: see uclibc
Notes: "This is a copy of the kconfig code in the kernel tweaked to suit uClibc" ([source](https://github.com/wbx-github/uclibc-ng/tree/master/extra/config))

Description: "The uClinux-dist source package is an "all-in-one" build framework for generating a complete system. It has been developed with embedded devices in mind, but it can just as equally be used for normal computing devices (like a PC for example). It is ideal for building small, lightweight systems." ([source](https://github.com/scs/uclinux/blob/master/README))
System Software: "The uClinux-dist was originally targeted specifically at non-MMU microprocessors. But for many years now it has supported full VM processors. It supports a wide varity of hardware, many CPUs and a large number of target boards." ([source](https://github.com/scs/uclinux/blob/master/README))
Notes: uses an unknown version of the Linux implementation

Description: "The Unikraft Library Operating System (LibOS) powers the next-generation of cloud native, containerless applications by enabling you to radically customize and build custom OS/kernels." ([source](https://unikraft.org/docs/getting-started))
System Software: "Unikraft addresses this need with its modular design, enabling developers to create customized, lightweight operating systems tailored to specific application requirements." ([source](https://github.com/unikraft/unikraft/blob/staging/README.md))
Notes: LKC is occasionally re-synced to the Linux implementation (currently [5.2](https://github.com/unikraft/unikraft/blob/ee652d8d94121e0099131c6a5b1d32c258ef781c/support/kconfig/README.unikraft)) applies [patches](https://github.com/unikraft/unikraft/tree/staging/support/kconfig/patches) to LKC

Description: "Xvisor is an open-source type-1 hypervisor, which aims at providing a monolithic, light-weight, portable, and flexible virtualization solution." ([source](https://github.com/xvisor/xvisor/blob/master/README.md))
System Software: "It provides a high performance and low memory foot print virtualization solution for ARMv7a-ve, ARMv8a, x86_64, RISC-V, and other CPU architectures. Xvisor primarily supports Full virtualization hence, supports a wide range of unmodified Guest operating systems." ([source](https://github.com/xvisor/xvisor/blob/master/README.md))
Notes: "For configuration Xvisor uses [Openconf](https://github.com/xvisor/xvisor/blob/master/tools/openconf/openconf_syntax.txt), which is a modified version of Linux Kconfig. The motivation behing Openconf is to get Xvisor specific information from environment variables, and to later extend the syntax of Kconfig to check for dependent libraries & tools at configuration time." ([source](https://github.com/xvisor/xvisor/blob/master/README.md)) uses a modified version of the Linux implementation at least as old as 2011 ([source](https://github.com/xvisor/xvisor/commit/26ade46b424e9de5f44cacfc6f46c3ba9fcee867))"

Description: "ACRN is a flexible, lightweight reference hypervisor, built with real-time and safety-criticality in mind, optimized to streamline embedded development through an open source platform." ([source](https://projectacrn.github.io/))
System Software: "ACRN is a type 1 reference hypervisor stack that runs on bare-metal hardware, with fast booting, and is configurable for a variety of IoT, Edge, and embedded device solutions." ([source](https://projectacrn.github.io/latest/introduction/index.html))
Notes: "Kconfiglib is used exclusively by e.g. the Zephyr, esp-idf, and ACRN projects." ([source](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/Kconfiglib)) "The ACRN hypervisor leverages Kconfig to manage configurations; it is powered by Kconfiglib." ([source](https://projectacrn.github.io/1.6.1/getting-started/building-from-source.html)) However, starting with v2.4, "Kconfig is no longer used for configuration. Related build targets, such as defconfig, now apply to the configuration files in XML." ([source](https://projectacrn.github.io/2.5/release_notes/release_notes_2.4.html))

Description: "Apache NuttX is a free and open-source (FOSS) real-time operating system (RTOS)" with "an emphasis on standards compliance and small footprint." ([source](https://nuttx.apache.org/))
System Software: "NuttX is a real-time operating system (RTOS) with an emphasis on standards compliance and small footprint. Scalable from 8-bit to 64-bit microcontroller environments, the primary governing standards in NuttX are POSIX and ANSI standards." ([source](https://nuttx.apache.org/docs/latest/))
Notes: "The Apache NuttX configuration system uses Linux's kconfig system which includes various frontends that allow you to modify configuration easily." ([source](https://nuttx.apache.org/docs/latest/quickstart/configuring.html)) "NuttX configuration system uses KConfig which is exposed via a series of interactive menu-based frontends, part of the kconfig-frontends package." "NuttX also supports kconfiglib by default, which is a Kconfig tool implemented in Python 2/3." ([source](https://nuttx.apache.org/docs/latest/quickstart/install.html))

Description: "ESP-IDF is the development framework for Espressif SoCs supported on Windows, Linux and macOS." ([source](https://github.com/espressif/esp-idf))
System Software: "Whether you are prototyping a sensor node, shipping a Matter-certified product, or building an edge device with AI, ESP-IDF gives you drivers, networking stacks, security features, and build tooling in one place so you can focus on your application." ([source](https://developer.espressif.com/tags/esp-idf/))
Notes: "Kconfiglib is used exclusively by e.g. the Zephyr, esp-idf, and ACRN projects." ([source](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/Kconfiglib)) "The esp-idf-kconfig package, originated in 2018, includes wider suite of tools, tailored for ESP-IDF, and is actively maintained. The package is designed to be used with the Espressif IoT Development Framework (ESP-IDF), although it can be used with other projects as well, either as a whole suite or as individual tools." ([source](https://docs.espressif.com/projects/esp-idf-kconfig/en/latest/kconfiglib/index.html)) "Although we tried to keep the esp-idf-kconfig package as close to the original kconfiglib as possible, there are some differences between the two." ([source](https://docs.espressif.com/projects/esp-idf-kconfig/en/latest/kconfiglib/differences.html))

Description: Huawei LiteOS is a lightweight operating system based on a real-time kernel, developed by Huawei for the Internet of Things (IoT). ([source](https://github.com/LiteOS/LiteOS))
System Software: Huawei LiteOS has enabled partners in the NB-IoT market through technology, ecosystem development, solutions, and commercial support, helping build an open-source IoT ecosystem. It has brought together more than 50 MCU and solution partners to develop open-source development kits and industry solutions. ([source](https://github.com/LiteOS/LiteOS))
Notes: imports KConfigLib ([source](https://github.com/LiteOS/LiteOS/blob/master/tools/menuconfig/usr_config.py))

Description: "MCUXpresso SDK is a comprehensive software enablement package designed to simplify and accelerate application development with Arm® Cortex®-M-based devices from NXP." ([source](https://github.com/nxp-mcuxpresso/legacy-mcux-sdk))
System Software: "This mcux-sdk project/repo provides the fundamental support for all NXP hot parts." ([source](https://github.com/nxp-mcuxpresso/legacy-mcux-sdk))
Notes: "In MCUXpresso SDK, Kconfig is used to config the build in runtime which includes component selection with dependency resolve, component configuration with feature enable, disable and customization." ([source](https://mcuxpresso.nxp.com/mcuxsdk/latest/html/develop/build_system/Configuration_System.html))

Description: "The goal of the OpenSBI project is to provide an open-source reference implementation of the RISC-V SBI specifications for platform-specific firmwares executing in M-mode." ([source](https://github.com/riscv-software-src/opensbi))
System Software: "An OpenSBI implementation can be easily extended by RISC-V platform and system-on-chip vendors to fit a particular hardware configuration." ([source](https://github.com/riscv-software-src/opensbi))
Notes: "All OpenSBI platforms support Kconfig style build-time configuration." ([source](https://github.com/riscv-software-src/opensbi))

Description: "PX4 is used in a wide range of use-cases, from consumer drones to industrial applications. It is also the leading research platform for drones and has been successfully applied to under water vehicles and boats." ([source](https://px4.io/))
System Software: "The PX4 Autopilot firmware can be configured at build time to adapt it for specialized applications (fixed-wing, multicopter, rover or more), to enable new and experimental features (such as Cyphal) or to save flash & RAM usage by disabling some drivers and subsystems." ([source](https://docs.px4.io/main/en/hardware/porting_guide_config))
Notes: "This configuration is handled through Kconfig, which is the same configuration system used by NuttX." ([source](https://docs.px4.io/main/en/hardware/porting_guide_config))

Description: "RIOT powers the Internet of Things like Linux powers the Internet. RIOT is a free, open source operating system developed by a grassroots community gathering companies, academia, and hobbyists, distributed all around the world." ([source](https://www.riot-os.org/))
System Software: "RIOT supports most low-power IoT devices, microcontroller architectures (32-bit, 16-bit, 8-bit), and external devices. RIOT aims to implement all relevant open standards supporting an Internet of Things that is connected, secure, durable & privacy-friendly." ([source](https://www.riot-os.org/))
Notes: "The objective of using Kconfig in RIOT is to configure software modules at compile-time." ([source](https://guide.riot-os.org/build-system/kconfig/))

Description: "RT-Thread is an open source IoT Real-Time Operating System (RTOS)." ([source](https://github.com/RT-Thread/rt-thread))
System Software: "RT-Thread is mainly written in C language, easy to understand and easy to port(can be quickly port to a wide range of mainstream MCUs and module chips)." "For resource-constrained microcontroller (MCU) systems, the Nano version that requires only 3KB Flash and 1.2KB RAM memory resources can be tailored with easy-to-use tools." ([source](https://github.com/RT-Thread/rt-thread))
Notes: "Its built-in menuconfig provides an easy-to-use configuration tailoring tool. It can tailor the kernels, components and software packages freely, so that the system can be constructed by building blocks." ([source](https://www.rt-thread.io/document/site/programming-manual/env/env/)) "env v2.0 require python kconfiglib" ([source](https://github.com/RT-Thread/env)) moved from kconfig-frontends to KConfigLib ([source](https://github.com/RT-Thread/rt-thread/blob/master/ChangeLog.md#tools-3))

Description: "The Zephyr Project is a scalable real-time operating system (RTOS) supporting multiple hardware architectures, optimized for resource constrained devices, and built with security in mind." ([source](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr))
System Software: "The Zephyr OS is based on a small-footprint kernel designed for use on resource-constrained systems: from simple embedded environmental sensors and LED wearables to sophisticated smart watches and IoT wireless gateways." ([source](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr)) The Zephyr kernel and subsystems can be configured at build time to adapt them for specific application and platform needs."" ([source](https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/build/kconfig/index.html))"
Notes: "Configuration is handled through Kconfig, which is the same configuration system used by the Linux kernel." ([source](https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/build/kconfig/index.html)) "Kconfiglib is used exclusively by e.g. the Zephyr, esp-idf, and ACRN projects." ([source](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/Kconfiglib))
